name: Moult Rat
description: The Moult Rat is identified by its deeply strange skin — it cycles through periods of rapid dermal shedding every six to eight weeks, during which it sheds a near-complete outer skin layer over 48-72 hours. The shed skin is not the dry scale-like shedding of reptiles but a coherent, slightly translucent membrane that peels in large patches and is left deliberately in specific locations by the animal. During active moulting periods, the Moult Rat's new skin is raw-looking and vivid pink-gray beneath, and the animal is unusually aggressive and pain-sensitive. The evolutionary driver is believed to be parasite load management — the rapid skin cycling makes sustained infestation extremely difficult. The rats are 4-5 kilograms, otherwise unremarkable in body plan, with a characteristic musty-sweet smell that persists in their territories.
diet: Omnivorous. Known to specifically seek out antiparasitic plant materials and certain industrial chemical residues that may support their skin cycling process.
notable_traits: Rapid full dermal shedding cycle every 6-8 weeks, leaving coherent shed membrane deposits in territory
Near-immunity to sustained ectoparasite infestation due to skin cycling
Heightened aggression during active moulting phase — normally timid animals become defensive and unpredictable
encounters: The shed skins are how most people first encounter Moult Rats — pale translucent patches found in corners, along wall bases, in cabinet backs. Finding shed Moult Rat skins in a building is considered a mixed omen in parts of the Shelf: bad because it means an infestation, somewhat reassuring because it means the rat is probably eliminating parasites that would otherwise find other hosts. Actual rat encounters during non-moulting periods are rare — moulting-phase encounters are alarming for the unexpected aggression.
known_uses: The shed skins have genuine medical applications in wound care — they have a documented mild antimicrobial and mechanical barrier property. Shelf district healers collect and process them. Helix Biosystems has reportedly been interested in the skin-cycling mechanism for years.
story_hooks: A healer whose entire practice depends on Moult Rat skin supplies is suddenly finding the colony she depended on has relocated — something changed in the building that drove them out, and she needs to know what
Someone is selling Moult Rat skin products as premium medical supplies to Tier 3 buyers — except they're not using genuine shed skins
